newsitem.title: HONG KONG: APT Satellite sets US$50 mln term loan.
newsitem.headline: APT Satellite sets US$50 mln term loan.

text.p: APT Satellite Holdings has mandated NatWest Markets to arrange a US$50 million term loan facility, NatWest Markets said on Thursday.
The loan has a final maturity of 18 months and will be available for drawing for six months.
Repayment is in two equal semi-annual installments commencing 12 months from the agreement date.
The loan pays a margin of 45 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate. Fees are 20 basis points for lead managers committing US$12.5 million, NatWest Markets said.
Proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.
NatWest said syndication will close on Friday. The facility already is oversubscribed, it said.

"The deal is well received by bankers whose exposures to the company had been significantly reduced as the previous project finance facilities related to the existing satellites were prepaid by proceeds from its IPO late last year," the arranger said in a statement.
Only a select number of APT's relationship banks were invited to participate in the facility, it said.
APT currently has two satellites in service and will launch its third later this year, NatWest Markets said.
